info.title: bria/image-edit-replace-background
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "bria/image-edit-replace-background", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Bria Background Replace API

example.prompt: A sunny beach with palm trees and a clear blue sky

enhance_ref_images.description: When true (default), extra processing of the reference images improves the result.

force_background_detection.description: When true, forces background detection and removal even if the input image has an alpha channel.

image.description: The image to edit. Supported input types are Base64-encoded string or URL pointing to a publicly accessible image file. Accepted formats JPEG, JPG, PNG, WEBP.

mode.description: The background generation mode, one of "base", "high_control" (default), or "fast". Applies only when prompt is provided.

negative_prompt.description: A text prompt specifying concepts, styles, or objects to exclude from the generated background.

original_quality.description: When true, the output keeps the original image size. When false (default), the output is scaled to 1MP.

prompt.description: A text description of the new background. Provide prompt or ref_images, not both. A hex color code in the prompt (for example, "#FF5733") produces a solid color background.

prompt_content_moderation.description: When enabled, applies content moderation to the prompt. Returns 422 if the prompt fails moderation.

ref_images.description: One reference image or a list of reference images that guide the background generation, each a Base64-encoded string or a URL pointing to a publicly accessible image file. Provide prompt or ref_images, not both.

refine_prompt.description: When true (default), the prompt is automatically adjusted for optimal generation results.

seed.description: Seed for deterministic generation. If omitted, a random seed is used.

sync.description:
When false (default), the request is processed asynchronously. When
true, the API holds the connection open until complete. ON COMFY
ROUTER that second mode is refused rather than forwarded: Router
fixes the return mode before dispatch and polls for the result
inside the call, so `POST /v2/models/bria/{model}` answers 422
invalid_input for any `sync` this route carries other than `false`
or `null` (routerForbiddenBodyFields). The synchronous call is
still available on this operation's own `/proxy/` route, which is
the surface this schema also describes.

visual_output_content_moderation.description: When enabled, applies content moderation to result visual. Returns 422 if the output fails moderation.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Bria models: the terminal `GET /v2/status/{request_id}` document, forwarded unchanged. Every Bria operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — the submit answers with a `BriaAsyncResponse` handle carrying `request_id`, and Router polls on the caller's behalf (`routerpollstate/families.go` `FamilyBria`), so the body a caller receives is the finished result rather than that handle. All nineteen Bria operations share this one status route and this one document shape.
WHICH FIELD CARRIES THE RESULT DEPENDS ON THE OPERATION, and it is the one thing a caller must not generalise from a sibling model's page. The fourteen image operations — `bria/fibo` and the thirteen `bria/image-edit-*` ids — put the edited image at `result.image_url`. The four `bria/video-edit-*` ids put the edited video at `result.video_url`. `bria/structured-instruction` fills neither URL: it returns the expanded prompt document at `result.structured_prompt`. `routerpollstate`'s `classifyBria` tests those three paths as alternatives, and each model's published example below shows the one its own operation fills.
`result` is present ONLY when `status` is `COMPLETED`, and it also carries `seed`, `prompt` and `refined_prompt`, which are echoes of the REQUEST rather than output — so a caller must key completion off the result LEAF for its operation rather than off `result` being non-empty. `routerpollstate` draws the same line: a `COMPLETED` whose `result` holds only those echoes is `success_without_output`, not a finished generation.
`status` is Bria's own UPPERCASE four-value vocabulary — `IN_PROGRESS`, `COMPLETED`, `ERROR`, `UNKNOWN` — and it is not case-folded. `error` is present only when `status` is `ERROR`.

error.description: Error object (only present when status is ERROR)

result.description: Result object (only present when status is COMPLETED)

refined_prompt.description: Refined version of the prompt, or null on a COMPLETED generation Bria did not refine. Nullable because the key is PRESENT carrying null rather than omitted; observed live on bria/image-edit-gen-fill.
